{
  "issue": 7258,
  "status": "needs_decision",
  "branch": "claude/issue-7258-chart-axis-count-i18n",
  "pr": null,
  "premise_still_valid": true,
  "summary": "The bug is real, but not fixable inside objectui without violating AGENTS.md #0.1 (contract-first). The literal 'Count' does NOT originate in the renderer: for a dataset-bound chart, DatasetWidget/ObjectChart pass queryDataset()'s res.fields straight into buildChartSeries() (packages/core/src/utils/chart-series.ts:441-442, labelOf), which trusts fields[].label as already-resolved author content -- exactly the behavior objectui#4106/ObjectChart.datasetMeasureLabel.test.tsx pins for a REAL custom measure label ('Tasks'). The English 'Count' is minted server-side in objectstack's service-analytics as a hardcoded default for the built-in count aggregate, with no i18n hook, at 5 sites: packages/services/service-analytics/src/analytics-service.ts:2045 and :2300 (inferMeasure), packages/services/service-analytics/src/cube-registry.ts:80 (inferFromObject), packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-create-seeds.ts:98, mirrored in packages/qa/downstream-contract/src/additional-domains.fixtures.ts:116. None of these are in objectui.",
  "tests": "No source changes made (diagnostic-only; no build/test run applicable). Evidence trail: grep -rn \"'Count'\" across objectui packages/ found only Studio config-panel enum labels (plugin-dashboard/src/index.tsx:242,318 -- authoring UI, not the rendered axis) and test fixtures -- no renderer-side literal that could produce a capitalized 'Count' axis title. Traced DatasetWidget.tsx:1390 (buildChartSeries(chartRows, dimensions, values, state.fields, ...)) and ObjectChart.tsx:848-856 (same helper) to core/src/utils/chart-series.ts:441-442, whose labelOf() falls back to the raw field NAME (lowercase 'count'), never a capitalized word -- ruling out a client-side humanizeLabel/humanizeFieldKey source (grep confirmed humanizeLabel is applied only to groupBy VALUES in ObjectChart.tsx:143/165, never to measure keys). Cross-referenced against objectstack (sibling checkout) and found the literal 'Count' hardcoded at the 5 producer sites listed in summary, all returning {name:'count', label:'Count', type:'count'} with no locale parameter. Confirmed existing CLIENT-side precedent for localizing this exact closed vocabulary purely by a structural discriminator: packages/i18n/src/locales/{en,zh}.ts 'report.aggregate.{count,sum,avg,min,max,...}' (zh: 'Count'->'计数') consumed by the pivot/matrix report, and 'grid.summary.{count,sum,avg,...}' (zh: 'Count'->'计数') consumed by packages/plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts -- both keyed by an explicit TYPE discriminator (ColumnSummaryType / report aggregate type), never by matching label text. Searched gh issue list on both repos for an existing duplicate (search: 'aggregate label i18n', 'measure label locale', 'aggregate label Count') -- objectui#4020/objectstack#5141 (axis showed raw NAME instead of label -- opposite direction, already fixed) and objectstack#4330/objectui#4575/#4566 (dimension-value and number-FORMAT locale, not aggregate-name TEXT) are related but distinct; no existing card covers this exact gap.",
  "mcp_calls": "0 -- all GitHub reads/writes used the gh CLI, not MCP GitHub tools",
  "open_questions": [
    {
      "question": "Where should the fix for the unlocalized default aggregate label ('Count'/'Sum'/'Avg'/...) land: a renderer-side heuristic in objectui, or a contract change in objectstack (service-analytics + spec) that objectui then consumes through its existing i18n seam?",
      "options": [
        "A. objectui infers 'this is a built-in aggregate' from the field NAME (e.g. name==='count') or from LABEL-TEXT matching ('Count'), then substitutes a locale string client-side, with no objectstack change.",
        "B. Extend the wire contract: add a structural discriminator to AnalyticsResult.fields[] in packages/spec/src/contracts/analytics-service.ts (objectstack) -- e.g. a builtinAggregate?: 'count'|'sum'|'avg'|'min'|'max'|'count_distinct' field -- populate it ONLY at the objectstack producer sites that currently hardcode the English default (analytics-service.ts:2045/2300, cube-registry.ts inferFromObject), leave it absent for any author-declared custom measure so 'Tasks'-style labels are untouched; queryDataset's REST response threads it through; objectui's buildChartSeries()/labelOf() then prefers a locale lookup keyed by that discriminator (reusing/mirroring the existing report.aggregate.* i18n keys) over the raw label, falling back to label when the discriminator is absent.",
        "C. Localize server-side: objectstack resolves the aggregate's display label by the request's exec.userLanguage (the channel already used for other server-generated user-visible strings per this repo's own doctrine) instead of a bare English literal, so the wire 'label' is already correct and objectui needs no change at all."
      ],
      "recommendation": "B, because long-term soundness (>=50% weight) rules out A outright: name-based inference ('count') risks silently clobbering a real author-named measure literally called 'count' with its OWN custom label, and label-text matching ('Count') breaks the instant the string is anything but that exact English literal (already-resolved non-English text, a renamed default, etc.) -- both are exactly the consumer-side leniency around a producer defect that AGENTS.md #0.1 forbids, and both duplicate a translation responsibility the codebase has already assigned to a STRUCTURAL discriminator twice (ColumnSummaryType for grid.summary.*, the report's own aggregate type for report.aggregate.*), never to label text or naming convention. B extends that exact, already-paid-for doctrine with one optional wire field and reuses an existing FE i18n namespace -- small, structurally sound, and hard for future AI-authored dataset/measure metadata to get wrong (real business need is confirmed by this issue's own repro; startup-scope discipline is satisfied because the diff is one optional field plus about three producer call sites plus one FE consumer, not new capability surface). C is the second choice if the maintainer prefers zero wire-contract change, but it duplicates the FE's is-this-my-language logic on the server and provides no discriminator for a future FE need (e.g. an author wanting to override just the built-in label per-widget); it is viable but a strictly worse fit for the existing architecture than B."
    }
  ],
  "out_of_scope_findings": []
}

PM ruling (maintainer 2026-09-02, in-session): **B — structural discriminator on the analytics contract**. The producer half is filed as objectstack-ai/objectstack#14492 (spec seat, Clause-②: yes). This card is the consumer half and stays parked until that lands.
